transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Korva Coleman.
The midterm elections are just one month from today.
Several new polls suggest Democrats have the advantage in several contests given President
Trump's unpopularity.
But it's not a given that they'll handily defeat Republican candidates.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro says that Democrats will also have to face the fact that their
party is also unpopular with many voters.
The unpopularity of the party could still dampen enthusiasm for some of those voters
who should lean in Democrats' direction.
More importantly, why these gains might be limited is the structure.
I mean, 25 of the 31 seats that Democrats are targeting are in places that Trump won
in 2024.
And as we know in this hyper-partisan era, it's just hard to go into places like that
and win in big numbers.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro reporting.
Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery are set to begin as a newly consolidated company
today.
NPR's Mandalit Dabrakko reports on what is being called the biggest merger in Hollywood
history.
David Ellison is growing his media empire with what will now be known collectively as
Skydance, which he secured for more than $111 billion.
The company merges two legendary movie studios, Paramount Pictures, and Warner Bros. Pictures.
Skydance also combines their streaming services, cable channels, and news outlets CNN and CBS
News.
The mega deal faced protests from actors, writers, and others worried about the concentration
of power and political interference.
But it ultimately passed legal and regulatory challenges in the U.S. and abroad.
Ellison is starting out with a huge debt, and those who fought to block the merger worry
there will be job cuts.
Mandalit Dabrakko, NPR News, Los Angeles.
The U.S. military has returned all of its long-range bombers from a British airbase
back to the U.S.
The move comes a week after British authorities arrested and briefly detained five men with
suspected ties to Iran near the airbase.
NPR's Greg Myry has more.
The U.S. military says all the bombers at Britain's Fairford airbase in the southwest
part of the country have returned to their home bases.
Vice President J.D.
Vance said the move was made out of an abundance of caution.
He also referred to Iranian acts of terrorism against U.S. targets in the past but did not
offer details on any new threats.
The U.S. has used the base to carry out airstrikes in the war against Iran.
Just over a week ago, British police arrested five young men near the base, raising suspicions
the facility might be a target.
However, the five have all been released on bail.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
You're listening to NPR.
This year's Nobel Prize in Physics has been awarded to Belgian physicist Francis Helzen.
He is being cited for contributions to finding out about particles that are high-energy neutrinos.
The Nobel Committee says he recognized that ice at the South Pole could be used to track
neutrinos.
His work has helped scientists study neutrinos that are spotted in the distant universe.
In the Canadian province of Quebec, a separatist party will lead the next provincial government.
Quebec is a French-speaking province.
Dan Carpentzak reports.
Partique ébécoileure Paul St. Pierre Plamondin had said he would call a referendum on Quebec
sovereignty during his first term if he won the election.
He has achieved a minority government, with his party taking 59 seats, the Liberals who
will now form the opposition with 40, the Conservatives 19, and the left-leaning Quebec
Solidaire 9.
Last night, Plamondin reassured English speakers that as Premier he would serve all the people
of Quebec, and to those in the rest of Canada, the project of independence is not against
them.
Plamondin also said he would work with those who stand up for Quebec, including Prime Minister
Mark Carney.
Carney, meanwhile, congratulated him on his victory, saying he was looking forward to
working with him to support the people and businesses of Quebec.
For NPR News, I'm Dan Carpentzak in Toronto.
Some AI experts testified before the New York City Council yesterday they're worried about
the dangers of the growing technology.
The Council is reviewing AI development, but AI company representatives pushed back.
They say they are fully focused on safety.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Democrats have advantage in midterm elections despite party unpopularity, but gains may be limited
Paramount, Skydance, and Warner Bros. Discovery complete merger into largest Hollywood consolidation, led by David Ellison
U.S. military returns long-range bombers from British Fairford airbase to U.S. following Iran-linked security concerns
Belgian physicist Francis Helzen awarded Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering high-energy neutrinos
Separatist Bloc Québécois wins Quebec provincial election with minority government under Paul St. Pierre Plamondin
AI experts testify to New York City Council about dangers of growing artificial intelligence technology
